classical_sentence: 环滁皆山也。
full_english: All around Chu are mountains.

full_english: A monk of the mountain, Zhixian.

title: 醉翁亭记

title: 出师表
meaning_in_this_sentence: 全国、整个天下

title: 出师表

full_english: You should humbly listen to opinions from all sides, extend the profound teachings left by the former emperor, and encourage the integrity of the conscientious and ambitious; and you should not belittle yourself or make unreasonable statements, which would block the communication channels with your loyal subjects.

full_english: In promotions and punishments, in praise and blame, there should be no difference: if any commit villainy and break the law, or prove loyal and good, they should be handed over to the officials in charge to determine their punishment or reward, so as to make plain Your Majesty's equitable and enlightened rule;

title: 出师表
meaning_in_this_sentence: 本句为动词『兴盛发达』（『兴复汉室』语境）
classical_sentence: 亲贤臣，远小人，此先汉所以兴隆也；
full_english: To be close to worthy ministers and keep petty men at a distance—this is why the Earlier Han flourished;

title: 出师表
meaning_in_this_sentence: （专名·待考）顿号并列的专名（山名／水名／县名），具体所指待查
classical_sentence: 侍中、尚书、长史、参军，此悉贞良死节之臣，愿陛下亲之信之，则汉室之隆，可计日而待也。
full_english: Palace Attendants, Imperial Secretaries, Chief Secretaries and Staff Officers—all these are loyal and upright ministers who would die for principle. I hope Your Majesty will draw close to them and trust them; then the rise of the Han house may be counted on by the day.

title: 出师表
meaning_in_this_sentence: 苟且保全（『苟全性命于乱世』）
classical_sentence: 臣本布衣，躬耕于南阳，苟全性命于乱世，不求闻达于诸侯。
full_english: I was originally a commoner, tilling my own fields at Nanyang, seeking only to preserve my life in troubled times, not striving to be known among the feudal lords.

title: 出师表
meaning_in_this_sentence: 拜访、探望（三顾臣于草庐之中），非『只是/回头看』

full_english: The late emperor did not disdain me for my humble status, humbled himself and visited the thatched cottage three times, asking me about the situation in the world, which made me very grateful, so I agreed to serve the late emperor and do my best.

title: 出师表
meaning_in_this_sentence: 劣马与钝刀，自喻才能平庸（谦辞）
classical_sentence: 今南方已定，兵甲已足，当奖率三军，北定中原，庶竭驽钝，攘除奸凶，兴复汉室，还于旧都。
full_english: Now that the south has been pacified and our arms and equipment are sufficient, I should encourage and lead the whole army north to pacify the Central Plain. I would fain exhaust my poor powers, root out the treacherous and the evil, restore the Han house, and return to the old capital.

title: 出师表
meaning_in_this_sentence: 本句为『斟情酌理、反复考虑』（『斟酌损益』）

title: 出师表

title: 桃花源记

full_english: During the Taiyuan period of the Jin Dynasty, there was a person in Wuling County who made a living by fishing.

full_english: Ask why, and they say: he and he are of similar age, and their learning alike.

title: 师说

title: 赤壁赋
meaning_in_this_sentence: 打鱼砍柴（『侣鱼虾而友麋鹿』语境『况吾与子渔樵于江渚之上』）
classical_sentence: 况吾与子渔樵于江渚之上，侣鱼虾而友麋鹿，驾一叶之扁舟，举匏尊以相属。
full_english: Moreover, you and I fish and gather wood on the river islets, companion to fish and shrimp, friend to elk and deer, sailing a single leaf of a boat, raising gourd cups to toast one another.

title: 赤壁赋
meaning_in_this_sentence: 片刻、一会儿（yú）
classical_sentence: 哀吾生之须臾，羡长江之无穷。
full_english: I mourn the brevity of my life, and envy the endless Yangtze.

title: 赤壁赋
meaning_in_this_sentence: 满（盈虚者如彼：月亮那样时圆时缺），非『士气饱满』
classical_sentence: 盈虚者如彼，而卒莫消长也。
full_english: that which waxes and wanes like that, yet in the end neither lessens nor grows.

title: 赤壁赋
meaning_in_this_sentence: 本句『彼竭我盈』谓士气枯竭
classical_sentence: 惟江上之清风，与山间之明月，耳得之而为声，目遇之而成色，取之无禁，用之不竭。
full_english: Only the clear breeze on the river and the bright moon between the hills, which the ear hears and makes sound, which the eye meets and makes colour—taking them none forbids, using them none exhausts.

title: 阿房宫赋
meaning_in_this_sentence: 天下、全国（古人以为中国四周环海）
classical_sentence: 六王毕，四海一，蜀山兀，阿房出。
full_english: The Six Kings ended, the Four Seas became one; the Shu hills were stripped bare, and Epang Palace rose.

title: 阿房宫赋
meaning_in_this_sentence: 秦都城（『聚之咸阳』）
classical_sentence: 骊山北构而西折，直走咸阳。
full_english: From Mount Li it stretched north, then bent west, running straight to Xianyang.

title: 阿房宫赋
meaning_in_this_sentence: 相斗（钩心斗角：屋角互相凑聚如相斗），非星宿名
classical_sentence: 各抱地势，钩心斗角。
full_english: each hugging the terrain, interlocking at heart and butting horn to horn.

title: 阿房宫赋
meaning_in_this_sentence: 楼阁之间的空中通道（『复道行空』）
classical_sentence: 复道行空，不霁何虹？
full_english: Sky-paths crossed the air—without rain clearing, whence the rainbow?

title: 阿房宫赋
meaning_in_this_sentence: 陪嫁的女子与宫女（yìng qiáng）
classical_sentence: 妃嫔媵嫱，王子皇孙，辞楼下殿，辇来于秦；
full_english: Consorts, concubines, princes and royal grandsons, bidding farewell to their towers and palaces, were carried by carriage to Qin;

title: 阿房宫赋
meaning_in_this_sentence: 含脂粉的洗面水
classical_sentence: 渭流涨腻，弃脂水也；
full_english: the greasy swell of the Wei River is the cast-off scented water;

title: 阿房宫赋
meaning_in_this_sentence: 听（辘辘远听：车声远远听来），非『准许』
classical_sentence: 辘辘远听，杳不知其所之也。
full_english: their rumble fading afar, vanishing none knew where.
note: 英译未直译『听』，以 rumble fading afar 承载

title: 阿房宫赋
meaning_in_this_sentence: 一旦：一天之间（一旦不能有：一天之间不能再保有），非『早晨』
classical_sentence: 一旦不能有，输来其间。
full_english: Once they could no longer be kept, they were carted here.

title: 阿房宫赋
meaning_in_this_sentence: 女子（机上之工女：织机上的女工），非通『汝』
classical_sentence: 架梁之椽，多于机上之工女；
full_english: the rafters of the beams outnumbered the weavers at their looms;

title: 阿房宫赋
meaning_in_this_sentence: 横的（直栏横槛：直的栏杆横的门槛），非『笼罩弥漫』
classical_sentence: 直栏横槛，多于九土之城郭；
full_english: straight rails and cross bars outnumbered the city walls of the Nine Regions;

title: 阿房宫赋
meaning_in_this_sentence: 戍守边疆的士兵（指陈涉起义），『戍卒叫』为跨词碎片
classical_sentence: 戍卒叫，函谷举，楚人一炬，可怜焦土！
full_english: Garrison soldiers cried out, Hangu Pass was taken, the men of Chu with one torch—alas, a pit of scorched earth!

title: 阿房宫赋
meaning_in_this_sentence: 灭亡、消灭（灭六国者：灭亡六国的人），『灭六国』为跨词碎片
classical_sentence: 灭六国者，六国也，非秦也。
full_english: He who destroyed the Six States was the Six States themselves, not Qin.

title: 六国论
meaning_in_this_sentence: 仗打得不好（善：擅长），『战不善』为跨词碎片
classical_sentence: 六国破灭，非兵不利，战不善，弊在赂秦。
full_english: The Six States fell not because their weapons were dull nor their fighting poor, but because their ruin lay in bribing Qin.

title: 六国论
meaning_in_this_sentence: 因为、由于（盖失强援：因为失去了强大的援助），非发语词
classical_sentence: 曰：不赂者以赂者丧，盖失强援，不能独完。
full_english: The answer: those who did not bribe were lost because of those who did; deprived of strong allies, they could not survive alone.

title: 六国论
meaning_in_this_sentence: 分封的各国君主，本句指受秦威胁的六国
classical_sentence: 则秦之所大欲，诸侯之所大患，固不在战矣。
full_english: So Qin's great desire and the lords' great peril lay not on the battlefield.

title: 六国论
meaning_in_this_sentence: 割让五座城（割：割让），『割五城』为跨词碎片
classical_sentence: 今日割五城，明日割十城，然后得一夕安寝。
full_english: Today cutting five cities, tomorrow ten, and only then gaining a single night's sound sleep.

title: 六国论
meaning_in_this_sentence: 本句为『灭亡』（『至于颠覆』），非今义『推翻』
classical_sentence: 至于颠覆，理固宜然。
full_english: As for utter overthrow, reason made it indeed inevitable.

title: 六国论
meaning_in_this_sentence: 割地贿赂秦国（赂：赠送财物求免），本句为六国论核心
classical_sentence: 齐人未尝赂秦，终继五国迁灭，何哉？
full_english: Qi never bribed Qin, yet in the end followed the five states into extinction. Why?

title: 六国论
meaning_in_this_sentence: 这（指示代词，『逝者如斯』）
classical_sentence: 是故燕虽小国而后亡，斯用兵之效也。
full_english: Hence Yan, though a small state, fell last—the effect of its use of arms.
term_english: the effect of its use of arms
note: 『斯』（这）英译未直译，以 the effect 承载

title: 六国论
meaning_in_this_sentence: 招致祸患（速：招致，古今异义）
classical_sentence: 至丹以荆卿为计，始速祸焉。
full_english: But when Dan resorted to the Jing Ke plot, calamity came swiftly.

title: 六国论
meaning_in_this_sentence: 本句为『命数、命运』（『则胜负之数，存亡之理』）
classical_sentence: 向使三国各爱其地，齐人勿附于秦，刺客不行，良将犹在，则胜负之数，存亡之理，当与秦相较，或未易量。
full_english: Had the three states each loved their land, had Qi not cleaved to Qin, the assassin not gone forth, the good general still stood—then victory or defeat, survival or ruin, matched against Qin, might well have proved otherwise.
note: 『数』（天数、命运）英译未单独体现

title: 六国论
meaning_in_this_sentence: 本句为『道理、情理』（『存亡之理』）
classical_sentence: 向使三国各爱其地，齐人勿附于秦，刺客不行，良将犹在，则胜负之数，存亡之理，当与秦相较，或未易量。
full_english: Had the three states each loved their land, had Qi not cleaved to Qin, the assassin not gone forth, the good general still stood—then victory or defeat, survival or ruin, matched against Qin, might well have proved otherwise.

title: 六国论
meaning_in_this_sentence: 全国、整个天下
classical_sentence: 以赂秦之地封天下之谋臣，以事秦之心礼天下之奇才，并力西向，则吾恐秦人食之不得下咽也。
full_english: Had the lands given to Qin been used to enfeoff the empire's strategists, and the heart that served Qin been turned to honour the empire's uncommon talents, with all strength turned westward, I fear the men of Qin could not have swallowed their meal.

title: 六国论
meaning_in_this_sentence: 治理国家的人（为：治理），『为国』为跨词碎片
classical_sentence: 为国者无使为积威之所劫哉！
full_english: Those who rule states—let them never be terrorised by accumulated might!

title: 过秦论
meaning_in_this_sentence: 古九州之一，秦据有其地（今陕西一带）
classical_sentence: 秦孝公据崤函之固，拥雍州之地，君臣固守以窥周室，有席卷天下，包举宇内，囊括四海之意，并吞八荒之心。
full_english: Duke Xiao of Qin, holding the fastness of Mount Xiao and the Hangu Pass and possessing the land of Yongzhou, with ruler and ministers firmly guarding it and eyeing the Zhou royal house, cherished the ambition to sweep up the world, wrap up the whole realm, gather in the four seas and swallow the eight wilds.

title: 过秦论
meaning_in_this_sentence: 八方荒远之地，指天下（『并吞八荒之心』）
classical_sentence: 秦孝公据崤函之固，拥雍州之地，君臣固守以窥周室，有席卷天下，包举宇内，囊括四海之意，并吞八荒之心。
full_english: Duke Xiao of Qin, holding the fastness of Mount Xiao and the Hangu Pass and possessing the land of Yongzhou, with ruler and ministers firmly guarding it and eyeing the Zhou royal house, cherished the ambition to sweep up the world, wrap up the whole realm, gather in the four seas and swallow the eight wilds.

title: 过秦论
meaning_in_this_sentence: 在这种情况下，因此
classical_sentence: 于是秦人拱手而取西河之外。
full_english: Therefore, Qin was as easily able to obtain the vast expanse of land west of the Yellow River as if it were using two hands to clap.

title: 过秦论
meaning_in_this_sentence: 本句为军事上险要之地（『北收要害之郡』）
classical_sentence: 孝公既没，惠文、武、昭襄蒙故业，因遗策，南取汉中，西举巴、蜀，东割膏腴之地，北收要害之郡。
full_english: After Duke Xiao died, King Huiwen, King Wu and King Zhaoxiang carried on the old enterprise and followed the bequeathed policy: south they took Hanzhong, west they seized Ba and Shu, east they cut off the fertile lands, north they gathered in the strategic commanderies.

title: 过秦论
meaning_in_this_sentence: 孟尝君，齐国公子，战国四公子之一（『齐有孟尝』）
classical_sentence: 当此之时，齐有孟尝，赵有平原，楚有春申，魏有信陵。
full_english: At that time Qi had Lord Mengchang, Zhao Lord Pingyuan, Chu Lord Chunshen, and Wei Lord Xinling.

title: 过秦论
meaning_in_this_sentence: 有所顾虑而徘徊不前（qūn xún）
classical_sentence: 秦人开关延敌，九国之师，逡巡而不敢进。
full_english: The men of Qin opened the pass to receive the enemy, yet the armies of the nine states hesitated and dared not advance.

title: 过秦论
meaning_in_this_sentence: 分割（分裂山河：分割国土山河）
classical_sentence: 因利乘便，宰割天下，分裂山河。
full_english: Turning advantage to profit, it carved up the world and split the rivers and mountains.

title: 过秦论
meaning_in_this_sentence: 本句『及至』即等到
classical_sentence: 及至始皇，奋六世之余烈，振长策而御宇内，吞二周而亡诸侯，履至尊而制六合，执敲扑而鞭笞天下，威振四海。
full_english: Then came the First Emperor: kindling the fierce legacy of six generations, he cracked the long whip to drive the universe, swallowed the Two Zhous and destroyed the lords, mounted the supreme throne and ruled the Six Directions, clutched the rod of chastisement and flogged the world—his might shook the four seas.

title: 过秦论
meaning_in_this_sentence: 把性命交托（『委命下吏』）
classical_sentence: 百越之君，俯首系颈，委命下吏。
full_english: the lords of the Baiyue bowed their heads, ropes about their necks, committing their lives to the petty officials.

title: 过秦论
meaning_in_this_sentence: 平民百姓（以黑巾裹头者）
classical_sentence: 于是废先王之道，焚百家之言，以愚黔首；
full_english: Then, Qin Shi Huang dispensed with the methods of governing the state used by previous kings, burned the books of the Hundred Schools of Thought, in order to create foolish common people.

title: 过秦论
meaning_in_this_sentence: 秦都城（『聚之咸阳』）
classical_sentence: 收天下之兵，聚之咸阳，销锋镝，铸以为金人十二，以弱天下之民。
full_english: collected the arms of the world, gathered them at Xianyang, melted blades and arrowheads, and cast them into twelve golden giants, thereby weakening the people of the world.

title: 过秦论
meaning_in_this_sentence: 本句为军事上险要之地
classical_sentence: 良将劲弩守要害之处，信臣精卒陈利兵而谁何。
full_english: Fine generals held strong bows, defending the most important places; reliable ministers led their crack troops, displaying their sharp weapons, and strictly interrogating whoever passed.

title: 过秦论
meaning_in_this_sentence: 不同的风俗，指边远地区（『余威震于殊俗』）
classical_sentence: 始皇既没，余威震于殊俗。
full_english: After the First Emperor died, his lingering might shook regions of different customs.

title: 过秦论
meaning_in_this_sentence: 本句通『影』，名词作状语，像影子一样（景从：如影随形）
classical_sentence: 斩木为兵，揭竿为旗，天下云集响应，赢粮而景从。
full_english: cutting wood for weapons, hoisting poles for banners, the world gathered like clouds and answered like echo, carrying grain to follow him as shadow follows form.

title: 过秦论
meaning_in_this_sentence: 本句『棘矜』指棘木做的戟柄（矜 qín：矛戟之柄，非『怜惜』）
classical_sentence: 锄櫌棘矜，非铦于钩戟长铩也；
full_english: hoe handles and thorn shafts were no sharper than hooked halberds and long spears;

title: 过秦论
meaning_in_this_sentence: 万辆兵车，代指天子大国
classical_sentence: 然秦以区区之地，致万乘之势，序八州而朝同列，百有余年矣；
full_english: Yet Qin, from a mere patch of ground, attained the might of ten thousand chariots, marshalled the eight provinces and made its fellow lords pay court, for more than a hundred years;

title: 廉颇蔺相如列传
meaning_in_this_sentence: 廉颇（者：语气词，表提顿），『廉颇者』为跨词碎片
classical_sentence: 廉颇者，赵之良将也。
full_english: Lian Po was Zhao's brilliant general.

title: 廉颇蔺相如列传
meaning_in_this_sentence: 人名，蔺相如，赵国上卿，本句为其行事主语
classical_sentence: 蔺相如者，赵人也，为赵宦者令缪贤舍人。
full_english: Lin Xiangru was a man of Zhao, a retainer of Miao Xian, Chief Eunuch of Zhao.

title: 廉颇蔺相如列传
meaning_in_this_sentence: 不给（勿：不），『欲勿予』为跨词碎片
classical_sentence: 欲勿予，即患秦兵之来。
full_english: to refuse, and they feared Qin's armies would come.

title: 廉颇蔺相如列传
meaning_in_this_sentence: 凭借什么（固定结构『何以战』，宾语前置）
classical_sentence: 对曰：“臣尝有罪，窃计欲亡走燕，臣舍人相如止臣，曰：‘君何以知燕王？
full_english: Miao Xian replied: 'I once committed a crime and secretly planned to flee to Yan. My retainer Xiangru stopped me, saying: Why do you...'

title: 廉颇蔺相如列传
meaning_in_this_sentence: 弱小（赵强而燕弱），非使动『削弱』
classical_sentence: 相如谓臣曰：‘夫赵强而燕弱，而君幸于赵王，故燕王欲结于君。
full_english: Xiangru told my messenger: 'Zhao is strong and Yan weak, and you enjoy the King of Zhao's favour, so the King of Yan wished to befriend you.'

title: 廉颇蔺相如列传
meaning_in_this_sentence: 通『否』（可予不：可以给他吗），『可予不』为跨词碎片
classical_sentence: 于是王召见，问蔺相如曰：“秦王以十五城请易寡人之璧，可予不？
full_english: Thereupon the king summoned Xiangru and asked: "The King of Qin offers fifteen cities for my jade—shall I give it?"

title: 廉颇蔺相如列传
meaning_in_this_sentence: 取走、拿走（取吾璧），『取吾璧』为跨词碎片
classical_sentence: 王曰：“取吾璧，不予我城，奈何？
full_english: The King of Zhao said, "But what if the King of Qin gets my treasure but doesn't give me the cities?"

title: 廉颇蔺相如列传
meaning_in_this_sentence: 给（不予赵城），『予赵城』为跨词碎片
classical_sentence: 赵予璧而秦不予赵城，曲在秦。
full_english: If Zhao gives the jade and Qin gives Zhao no cities, the fault lies with Qin.

title: 廉颇蔺相如列传
meaning_in_this_sentence: （专名·朝代名）本句以朝代为主语，叙述其政治地理沿革
classical_sentence: 秦王坐章台见相如，相如奉璧奏秦王。
full_english: The King of Qin sat on the Zhangtai stage to meet Lin Xiangru and Lin Xiangru offered the He Shi Bi to the King of Qin.

title: 廉颇蔺相如列传
meaning_in_this_sentence: 说（乃前曰）
classical_sentence: 相如视秦王无意偿赵城，乃前曰：“璧有瑕，请指示王。
full_english: Lin Xiangru saw that the King of Qin had no intention of giving a city to Zhao in exchange for the stone, so he stepped forward and said, "There is a tiny flaw in this magnificent stone. Please allow me to show it to Your Majesty."

title: 廉颇蔺相如列传
meaning_in_this_sentence: 在这个时候／在此地（词组）
classical_sentence: 于是赵王乃斋戒五日，使臣奉璧，拜送书于庭。
full_english: So the King of Zhao fasted five days, had me bear the jade, and solemnly sent the letter of gift in the courtyard.

title: 廉颇蔺相如列传
meaning_in_this_sentence: 得到璧玉，『得璧』为跨词碎片
classical_sentence: 得璧，传之美人，以戏弄臣。
full_english: you got the jade and passed it among your beauty-maids, to make sport of me.

title: 廉颇蔺相如列传
meaning_in_this_sentence: 道歉（乃辞谢固请），非『感谢/凋谢』
classical_sentence: 秦王恐其破璧，乃辞谢固请，召有司案图，指从此以往十五都予赵。
full_english: The King of Qin was afraid that he would smash the jade to pieces, so he apologized, earnestly begged him not to, and summoned the officials in charge to examine the map, pointing out the fifteen cities from one place to another to be handed over to Zhao.

title: 廉颇蔺相如列传
meaning_in_this_sentence: (duó)推测、估计（『相如度秦王特以诈』）
classical_sentence: 相如度秦王特以诈详为予赵城，实不可得，乃谓秦王曰：“和氏璧，天下所共传宝也，赵王恐，不敢不献。
full_english: Xiangru guessed that the King of Qin would only use fraud to pretend to give the State of Zhao a city, but in fact it would be impossible for the State of Zhao to get it, so he said to the King of Qin: "He Shi Bi" is a treasure recognized by the world. The King of Zhao is afraid of your country and does not dare not to offer it.

title: 廉颇蔺相如列传
meaning_in_this_sentence: (duó)推测、估计（『相如度秦王特以诈』）
classical_sentence: 秦王度之，终不可强夺，遂许斋五日，舍相如广成传。
full_english: The King of Qin weighed the matter, after all, it cannot be taken by force, so he agreed to fast for five days, and asked Xiangru to stay in the Guangcheng guesthouse.

title: 廉颇蔺相如列传
meaning_in_this_sentence: 不交出城邑作为补偿，『不偿城』为跨词碎片
classical_sentence: 相如度秦王虽斋，决负约不偿城，乃使其从者衣褐，怀其璧，从径道亡，归璧于赵。
full_english: Xiangru guessed that although the King of Qin agreed to fast, he must break his promise and not give the city, so he sent his entourage to put on coarse linen clothes, hide the treasure in his arms, and escaped from the small road, sending the treasure back to the State of Zhao.

title: 廉颇蔺相如列传
meaning_in_this_sentence: 臣下对君主的尊称，本句为外交辞令中的秦王
classical_sentence: 且秦强而赵弱，大王遣一介之使至赵，赵立奉璧来。
full_english: Besides, Qin is strong and Zhao is weak. If Your Majesty sends an envoy to Zhao, Zhao will immediately send the treasure-jade.

title: 送东阳马生序
meaning_in_this_sentence: 特别爱好学习（嗜：酷爱）
classical_sentence: 余幼时即嗜学。
full_english: In my youth I was already fond of learning. My family was poor and could not obtain books to read, so I often borrowed from families with collections, copied them out by hand, and counted the days to return them on time. In bitter cold the ink froze solid in the inkstone and my fingers could neither bend nor stretch, yet I did not slacken. When the copying was done I hurried to return the books, never daring to exceed the agreed term by a hair. That is why most people were willing to lend me books, and so I was able to read widely. After coming of age I admired the way of the sages all the more, yet worried that I had no profound masters or famous men to keep company with. I once hurried a hundred li to question a learned elder of my home region, clasping the classics. The elder was of high renown; his disciples filled his room, and he never softened his words or countenance the slightest degree. I stood in attendance, raised doubts and questioned principles, bending down with ears intent; when I met his rebukes my manner grew more respectful, my courtesy more scrupulous, not daring to utter a word in reply; when he grew pleased I would ask again. Thus, dull as I was, I in the end gained real instruction.

title: 送东阳马生序
meaning_in_this_sentence: 鞋（xǐ，『负箧曳屣』）
classical_sentence: 当余之从师也，尝负箧曳屣，行深山巨谷中。
full_english: When I went to seek my teachers I carried book-boxes on my back and trailed shoes through deep mountains and great valleys. In deep winter, under fierce wind and snow several feet deep, the skin of my feet cracked without my noticing. On reaching the lodge, my limbs were frozen stiff and would not move; the serving maid poured hot water over me and wrapped me in quilts, and only after a long while did warmth return. Lodging at the inn, the host gave two meals a day, with nothing fresh or rich to enjoy. My fellow lodgers wore embroidered silks and caps hung with pearl tassels and jewels, girdles of white jade, a knife at the left, a scent-bag at the right, radiant as gods. I, in worn padded gown and ragged clothes, dwelt among them without the least envy, for what sufficed to make me happy was within: I did not feel my food and clothing inferior. Such were the toil and hardship of my studies. Now, though old with nothing achieved, I have luckily joined the ranks of gentlemen, enjoying the Emperor's glorious favour, trailing behind dukes and ministers, daily in attendance for consultation, and my name is, undeservedly, known across the realm — how much more those whose talent surpasses mine!

meaning_in_this_sentence: 官府供给的粮食（廪稍之供）
classical_sentence: 今诸生学于太学，县官日有廪稍之供，父母岁有裘葛之遗，无冻馁之患矣；
full_english: Now the students study at the Imperial Academy: the government supplies daily grain, parents send yearly winter and summer clothing, so there is no fear of cold and hunger; they sit beneath great halls reciting the Songs and Documents, with no toil of running about; Assistant Supervisors and Erudites serve as their teachers — none asks without being told, none seeks without obtaining; all the books one ought to have are gathered here, with no need, like mine, to copy by hand or borrow from others before seeing them. meaning_in_this_sentence: 本句『称』为称许、称赞（非『著称』）
classical_sentence: 东阳马生君则，在太学已二年，流辈甚称其贤。
full_english: Ma Junze of Dongyang has been at the Academy for two years, and his contemporaries greatly praise his worth. When I came to the capital for audience, the young man called on me as a fellow-provincial junior, presenting a long letter as his gift, its style fluent and lucid; in debate with him his words were mild and his countenance even. He says that in his youth he laboured hard at learning — he may truly be called a good learner. As he is about to return home to see his parents, I therefore tell of the difficulty of learning to instruct him.
